post.caption: Beeswax reattached this gold mask's beard. The mask covered Tutankhamun's mummy when Howard Carter's team found it in 1925. A German and Egyptian team reattached the beard with beeswax in 2015. The mask is about 21 inches tall and weighs over 22 pounds, and it is made from two hammered sheets of gold joined together. The eyes are quartz with obsidian, and lapis lazuli adds deep blue. The cobra and vulture on the brow represent Lower and Upper Egypt. Its back carries a protective spell from the Book of the Dead. Today it is on display at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza.
